prompt: After feedback on her talk, Ines rewrites the script, redesigns every slide, slows her pace, and practises in a different room — all at once. The next talk goes better, but she has no idea which change helped, and one change may even have hurt. What would have given her usable knowledge, not just a better talk?

options.text: Changing even more things next time, so the improvement is bigger and easier to see
Changing one or two linked things at a time and comparing the result, so she can tell what actually made the difference
Asking the audience afterwards which change they think helped most, and trusting that completely
Keeping a list of everything she changed, which on its own tells her which one worked

explanation: When everything changes at once, improvement cannot be attributed to any single change — and a harmful change can hide inside a good overall result. Testing changes in small steps builds knowledge she can reuse in every future talk.
